description: Sabotages only the documentation examples catch. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format. testArgs has no --lib because the harness cannot pre-build doctests: the suite runs whole, so it is kept to the entries only a doctest can see.

sabotages.name: SqEntry is no longer non_exhaustive
sabotages.why: TW-D-6: a further kind of entry must not break a caller. The only thing that fails when the attribute goes is a caller written outside the crate, which a documentation example is.

sabotages.name: control: the entry kinds are declared in another order
sabotages.why: The order of the variants is not a promise, and nothing matches on it.

sabotages.name: ReadEntry is no longer non_exhaustive
sabotages.why: A further kind of entry must not break a client. The only thing that fails when the attribute goes is a caller written outside the crate, which a documentation example is.

sabotages.name: Watcher::register_with is made public
sabotages.why: The reading layer attaches what a read needs through it, and a caller does not: the watcher's public surface does not grow (TW-9.4). Only an example written outside the crate sees it.

sabotages.name: Watcher::stop_handle is made public, with the type it returns
sabotages.why: It is how the layer requests shutdown from where it holds only a handle. The method and its return type are made public together, as a real widening of the surface would be: a public method returning a crate-private type cannot be used from outside, which would make the example fail to compile for a reason that has nothing to do with the method.
find: /// See [`Watcher::stop_handle`]. It keeps the watcher's shared state, files included, alive, so an
/// owner drops it with the watcher.

sabotages.name: Watcher::mark_terminal is made public
sabotages.why: A read, and not a probe, marks a registration terminal through it.

sabotages.why: The layer reports through the watcher's sink with it.
